problem: The chapter says "the shorter direction usually has the larger moment per metre". This is reversed. Both directions cantilever from the column face, and Mu = wu l²/2 per metre width, so the direction with the longer projection has the larger moment per metre. In a rectangular pad L × B with L > B, the projection (L − b)/2 is the longer one, so the long direction carries the bigger moment per metre.
fix: "Check both directions. The longer projection gives the larger moment per metre, so the direction of the longer side of the pad usually needs more steel; the shorter direction needs less."

problem: The units do not match the formula shown. The box says Pu is in N, A in m² (so wu comes out in N/m², not N/mm²), wu is in N/mm² "when used with mm", l is in m, and Mu is in N·mm. With wu in N/mm² and l in m, wu l²/2 is not N·mm per metre. The worked example actually uses wu in kN/m² and l in m to get kN·m per metre, which is correct but contradicts the box.
fix: "Pu is factored column load in kN; A is plan area in m²; wu = Pu/A is in kN/m²; l is the projection in m; Mu = wu l²/2 is in kN·m per metre width (multiply by 10⁶ to get N·mm); fck is in N/mm²; b is taken as 1000 mm and d comes out in mm."

problem: In "lx = (L − b)/2 and ly = (B − c)/2" the symbols b and c are not defined. Earlier, c meant the side of a square column, so a reader cannot tell which column dimension goes with which pad side.
fix: "For a rectangular pad, take b as the column side parallel to L and c as the column side parallel to B, so lx = (L − b)/2 and ly = (B − c)/2."

problem: Z is introduced only as "section modulus in m³" with no formula, so a student cannot compute pmax or pmin for a real pad.
fix: Add: "For a rectangular pad of sides L and B, bending about the axis parallel to B gives Z = BL²/6 in m³; use the axis about which the moment acts."

problem: The figure note says "all three checks use the same factored upward pressure", which suggests the worked example carries out bending, one-way shear and punching. The worked example stops after the bending depth.
fix: "The factored upward pressure wu is the same for the bending, one-way shear and punching checks (worked example covers sizing and bending depth only)."
